problem.observed: Dev Taiwan Market Daily Refresh (force=true, 2026-10-08T09:10Z) logged 'bounded source refresh prioritizing active paper symbols: 2330.TW', then 'bounded source refresh service source-ingest-scheduler exited with code 1'. It was the first time the hosted refresh ran the bounded path; every earlier run had skipped with no_active_taiwan_symbols.
problem.readback: Hosted /data/source-ingest/bounded-refresh/controller_state.json (read-only): last_failure_stage=controller, last_failure_reason="ControllerLeaseConflict: Active lease exists for loop 'source_ingestion'; fenced owner is controller 'source-ingestion-1c877c903a1f:c97d2852aa40', so the stale or foreign writer was rejected." 1c877c903a1f is the steady source-ingest-scheduler container.
problem.cause: execute_bounded_source_refresh_entrypoint stops the steady scheduler with docker stop and starts the one-shot bounded scheduler about 80 seconds later. The steady controller's loop-control lease is 2 x interval (120 s on hosted) and LoopControllerStore has no release, so the bounded controller arrived while the lease was still active and was rejected as a foreign writer.

change: After the steady scheduler is stopped, the refresh waits until that controller's lease must have expired before starting the bounded run. The lease is SOURCE_INGEST_CONTROLLER_LEASE_SECONDS from the steady container environment, else twice its SOURCE_INGEST_CONTROLLER_INTERVAL_SECONDS (default 60), plus one second, minus the time already spent since the stop.

The one-shot bounded scheduler and projector run with SOURCE_INGEST_CONTROLLER_INTERVAL_SECONDS=10, as in the isolated L12 harness pull. Their lease is therefore 20 s, so the restored steady scheduler is fenced for at most one tick.
unchanged: Preflight, symbol resolution, egress allowlist and restore, image identity guards, bounded container names, the steady-service stop/start protections from DEV-TW-REFRESH-STEADY-SERVICES-20261008 and readback verification are unchanged. Without a steady scheduler the refresh already refuses earlier (steady_scheduler_deploy_values_missing), so the wait is only computed when steady containers exist.
test_changes: The stub docker records event times and docker stop. The steady scheduler environment comes from the stub state and defaults to a one-second interval, which keeps existing tests to a ~3 s wait.

New tests: test_refresh_waits_for_stopped_steady_lease_before_bounded_run (explicit lease 3 s gives a stop-to-run gap of at least 3 s); test_refresh_lease_wait_defaults_to_twice_steady_interval (interval 2 s and no lease gives a gap of at least 4 s); test_bounded_refresh_one_shot_uses_ten_second_controller_interval.
